chunks: And from him, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the two sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever vomits intentionally while he is fasting, he must make up one day in its place."
ai.seo_question: Does intentional vomiting break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the distinction between intentional and unintentional vomiting in the context of fasting. The ruling specifies that only deliberate vomiting breaks the fast, necessitating a make-up day (*qada*), while accidental vomiting does not, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of ease in ritual obligations. This hadith is foundational in the chapter on medical treatments for the fasting, emphasizing that the act must be willful to invalidate the fast.
